items.title: (Nog?) geen concrete interesse in Trenskow: 'Had verwacht dat er nu iets zou zijn'
items.summary: Jacob Trenskow (25) maakte vorig seizoen liefst zestien doelpunten voor SC Heerenveen, kreeg een uitnodiging voor de Deense nationale ploeg en werd genomineerd voor de prijs Eredivisie Speler van het Jaar. Ook deze voorbereiding is hij weer in goeden doen: vorige week maakte Trenskow twee goals tegen Club Brugge (2-3 zege) en zaterdag was hij tegen Leuven goed voor een hattrick (4-4). Toch is er nog altijd geen concrete interesse in hem.

items.title: Trial to be introduced in bid to prevent goalkeeper tactical time-outs
items.summary: Measures planned to run throughout 2026-27 season Ifab yet to give permission for proposed rule change English football will introduce a trial this season in an effort to end the goalkeeper tactical time-out. The trial – backed collectively by Pro Ref, the Football Association, Premier League, English Football League, Women’s Super League and the National League – aims to prevent goalkeeper injuries used to disrupt momentum and allow opportunities for tactical instruction. items.title: Mind the ever-growing gap: the Premier League keeps spending big
items.summary: English clubs have spent more on players this summer than the other four major European leagues combined The financial power of the Premier League is unmatched. The teams in England’s top division have collectively invested more than £1.4bn in new players already this summer (through disclosed fees alone), around £303m more than the 76 clubs from the Bundesliga, La Liga, Ligue 1 and Serie A combined. These figures are the gross spend, so take no account of players sold to help balance the books. Factoring this in only increases the divide. The clubs of Ligue 1 and the Bundesliga are £203.4m and £72.2m in credit from their transfer dealings respectively. While La Liga (£163.1m) and Serie A (£124.1m) have spent more than they have earned, they are an ocean adrift of the Premier League’s net spend of £523.6m. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Born out of quality’: Webb vows to increase match officials from minority groups
items.summary: Referees’ body stands by diversity initiatives Webb believes diverse talent pool will ‘raise standards’ Howard Webb, England’s chief refereeing officer, has vowed to continue increasing the talent pool from under-represented communities in English football’s officiating pathway, rejecting the wider backlash against diversity initiatives. Addressing that historic under-representation has prompted a new direction. In June, the newly named Professional Referees’ Body (Pro Ref), formerly called Professional Game Match Officials, announced that Select Group 1, 2 and its supplementary list had been merged into a new, single Professional Referee Group in the men’s professional game and will largely service the Premier League and the Championship from the start of the 2026-27 season. Pro Ref said it would create flexibility in appointments and help to recognise a wider variety of talented match officials as part of the organisation’s new direction. Continue reading...

items.title: Chelsea explore surprise move to sign Danny Welbeck from Brighton
items.summary: Veteran scored 13 goals in 37 league games last season Interest signals shift in Stamford Bridge transfer strategy Chelsea are understood to be in talks over a move to sign Danny Welbeck from Brighton. Welbeck is a surprise candidate to bolster Xabi Alonso’s forward line after scoring 13 goals in 37 Premier League match last season, and there is optimism at Stamford Bridge that a deal can be concluded with Brighton understood to be willing to allow the 35-year-old striker, who has a year remaining on his contract, to leave for the right price. Rodri’s terms expire next June and he has failed to sign City’s new deal, which has been on the table for a while.
